title: openai-compat: tool_choice semantics, tool schema mapping, and tool message formatting
author: Ava Martinez
description: Context: This PR finalizes a set of changes to the OpenAI compatibility layer to 1) standardize tool_choice semantics to match OpenAI's documented behavior when multiple tools are eligible, 2) introduce a bidirectional mapping between Redwood ToolSchema and OpenAI-style JSON Schema parameters, and 3) normalize tool->assistant message formatting so tool outputs are represented consistently across streaming and non-streaming flows. Motivation: Customers integrating Redwood via the OpenAI-compatible surface were seeing divergence in tool selection behavior and inconsistent message formatting (role names, metadata placement), which caused downstream SDK and eval mismatches. This change reduces interoperability issues and enables existing OpenAI-based client code to work with fewer shims. Summary of changes: - Implemented tool_choice semantics: explicit "tool_choice" envelope emitted for ambiguous decisions and a deterministic tie-breaker policy (priority then recency). - Tool schema mapping: added a mapping layer that converts Redwood ToolSchema fields (type, enum, required, description, examples) to OpenAI "parameters" JSON Schema and vice versa for responses. Mapping preserves Redwood metadata via x-redwood-* prefixed annotations. - Tool message formatting: unify tool response messages to use role="tool" with standardized metadata keys (tool_name, tool_version, provenance) in message.metadata; stream fragments now include consistent metadata frames to allow SDKs to reassemble tool outputs reliably. - Backwards compat: default compatibility mode preserves existing behavior; new strict_openai_mode flag enables full OpenAI semantics. - Tests: added unit tests for schema round-trips, end-to-end integration tests for a 3-tool routing scenario, and recorded fixture updates for TS/Python SDKs. - Docs: updated redwood-docs openai-compat guide with mapping table and migration notes. Migration notes: No breaking changes by default. Customers wanting exact OpenAI parity should enable strict_openai_mode in their service config or set the OPENAI_COMPAT_STRICT env var; SDKs were patched to enable the flag for v0.24+ clients. Checklist: - [x] Spec and design doc linked (ENG-1258) - [x] Unit & integration tests - [x] SDK update patches (python + typescript) - [x] Docs and release notes - [x] QA smoke on dedicated and hosted staging Testing and validation: ran full CI, initial integration run surfaced an intermittent ordering race in streaming fragments which was fixed by adding a fragment-sequence header and an assembly test; load tests show negligible latency overhead (~0.8ms median per-call) when strict_openai_mode is enabled. Release notes: Adds opt-in strict OpenAI function/tool calling compatibility: tool_choice deterministic tie-breaking, schema mapping for tool parameters, and normalized tool message formatting. See migration notes in docs.
